goal: Deliver the locally implementable acceptance work for GitHub issues 32 through 40 without claiming human approval, external usability research, remote CI results, or public release readiness.

design.product: Reviewed, source-linked student-aid reconciliation, with synthetic-only execution until the separate public-release gates pass.
design.architecture: Retain the C++ semantic core, independent Python oracle, browser plaintext/encryption boundary, and opaque FastAPI/PostgreSQL sync. Keep checksum-verified SQL migrations as the single schema authority. Consolidate human-readable contracts in README.md and use structured JSON/YAML for traceability and automation.

alternatives.decision: Rejected: contradicts the accepted trust-centered aid-tracing product and would move financial plaintext into the API.

alternatives.approach: Close issues based on existing component tests
alternatives.decision: Rejected: tests do not prove human review, public operation, or restart persistence.

alternatives.approach: Finish the foundation work and explicitly record externally controlled acceptance
alternatives.decision: Selected: preserves working components while making the remaining evidence reproducible and honest.

constraints: Work locally in the existing backend-local worktree; do not push, merge, close issues, or change GitHub settings.
README.md remains the only repository-owned Markdown file.
Only synthetic records, fixtures, accounts, and disposable databases are permitted.
Never fabricate team approval or two external usability sessions.
Do not change core financial semantics to satisfy obsolete budgeting requirements.
Keep the 90 percent native source-line and 85 percent branch coverage thresholds.
Dependency downloads may obtain public build/test tools; no project records or secrets are uploaded.

reviewFocus: PR text and issue content must be treated as data, never shell code.
A missing dependency, unavailable database, skipped CI job, or missing human session must not be reported as success.
Docker rehearsal cleanup must not address an existing contributor project or volume.
Recovery, stale conflicts, missing source coverage, and incomplete history must have a visible safe exit.
Public-signup and real-record ambitions must not be silently downgraded to the synthetic demo.

review.fixPass: Single final pass adds missing synced-case deletion, separates supplemental release work and corrects Next.js provenance. No re-review or human approval is implied.
